messages.subject: error message from bootstrap
parts:
I am running DISTANCE 5.0 release 2 and trying to get bootstrap =
estimates of variance. I am having some of my runs terminated with what =
appears to be a fatal bootstrap error. At the top of the LOG is the =
following:
=20
Initializing=20

Making Data File=20

Making Data Selection Queries=20

Making Input File=20

Engine started with the following command:

C:\PROGRA~1\DISTAN~2\ec "C:\PROGRA~1\DISTAN~2\MCDS.exe 0, =
C:\DOCUME~1\ERICD~1.STO\LOCALS~1\Temp\dst12F9.tmp \options =
2>C:\DOCUME~1\ERICD~1.STO\LOCALS~1\Temp\dst12F8.tmp"=20

** Error: Analysis engine terminated unexpectedly (with error code =
-2147483576). **

-- Start of Analyis Engine Log File --=20

At the bottom of the LOG file there is the following:

** Bootstrap Error: Negative variance estimate for f(0). Invalid =
variance. **

Note: Size bias adjustment would have increased expected cluster size.

-- End of Analyis Engine Log File --=20

** Warning: Analysis engine wrote some output to the console error =
stream, reproduced below. **

-- Start of Console Error Stream --=20

forrtl: error (72): floating overflow Image PC Routine Line Source=20

MCDS.exe 00439BC3 DFSATTER 428 Dmod.for

MCDS.exe 0044A4CE CMBSTR 1115 Estmte.for

MCDS.exe 0044764C ESTPARM 487 Estmte.for

MCDS.exe 00446596 ESTMTE 311 Estmte.for

MCDS.exe 00401561 BOOTSTRAP 85 Boot.for

MCDS.exe 00445259 ESTPROC 96 Estmte.for

MCDS.exe 004136DA CNTRL 113 Control.for

MCDS.exe 004381BF DISTANCE 263 Distance.for

MCDS.exe 004F2479 Unknown Unknown Unknown

MCDS.exe 004C8C03 Unknown Unknown Unknown

kernel32.dll 7C816FD7 Unknown Unknown Unknown

-- End of Console Error Stream --=20

Analysis engine status 'Run failed - analysis engine encountered an =
unknown error, possibly in the input or output files'=20

Reading Results=20

Run finished=20

=20
I'm not sure what to do next - any ideas would be greatly appreciated.
=20
=20
Eric Stolen, Ph.D.
Wildlife Ecologist
Dynamac Corp.

From: Wildlife abundance estimation using distance sampling techniques. =
on behalf of Jeff Laake
Sent: Fri 5/16/2008 6:25 PM
To: DISTANCE...@JISCMAIL.AC.UK
Subject: Re: [DIST-SAMP] g(0) estimation for bottlenose dolphin aerial =
surveys



Wendy-

You seem to have a fairly good understanding of the problem. Your
front/back idea will work as long as
you are correct that they time difference is longer than the longest
period of unavailability. If not then
the other ways this has been approached are:
1) using estimate of availability but not just time at surface as you =
note
2) combined land-based aerial observations (see Laake et al 1997 in JWM,
also ref to Kraus et al)
3) tandem aircraft (Hiby and Lovell Biometrics) and single aircraft with
tandem surveys (Caretta et al MMS)

Also, there is a recent paper that discusses some of these issues.=20
You'll also find many of the references in ch6 of the Advanced Distance
Sampling book.

Pollock, K. H., Marsh, H. D., Lawler, I. R., and Alldredge, M. W.
(2006). Estimating animal abundance in heterogeneous environments: An
application to aerial surveys for Dugongs. Journal of Wildlife
Management 70, 255-262.

I'll send some of the above papers in a separate email.

regards --jeff

Wendy Noke wrote:
> > We have been conducting line transect aerial surveys for bottlenose
> > dolphins within a shallow estuary system and are interested in
> > evaluating g(0) for our study area. Given that the estuary is very
> > shallow in nature (average depth =3D 1m), we think that availability =
bias
> > is small since we can see the animals in shallow water and when they =
are
> > at the surface. In our study area availability bias can be attributed
> > to animals being submerged in the deeper dredged channels, where we =
can
> > not see to the bottom. We are contemplating utilizing mark-recapture
> > distance sampling to evaluate availability bias. Specifically we are
> > interested in using the trial-observer method where the front observer
> > looks ahead and sets up experiments to see if the back observer sees =
the
> > animal as well (both observers would be isolated visually and
> > acoustically). We believe that the short surfacing interval for these
> > shallow estuarine animals will allow the front and back observers to
> > view the same animal during different surfacing cycles. We are
> > wondering how others have addressed similar concerns of availability
> > bias in marine mammals with short surfacing durations. We have also
> > given some thought to utilizing surfacing data (we have some available
> > for a small number of radio-tagged animals) to address availability
> > bias, however we feel that this may not be completely applicable since
> > animals are often "available" for sighting even when submerged. Any
> > suggestions or advice based on previous experience with mark-recapture
> > models for line transect surveys would be greatly appreciated.
> >
> > Thank you for your time.
> >
